mathematical_sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03, when the entry and its discussion thread recorded no proof claims. Bloom's catalog entry supplies the problem number and statement.

mathematical_sources.note: At commit 7bdc4a42f24c0316f81c73b26121794b2bed96a3. The definition of f in Challenge.lean is copied verbatim, and so is that of SimpleGraph.IsCliqueEdgePartition, from FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Chordal.lean at the same commit. The proof development repeats both with their proved API. erdos_1017.lower_bound and erdos_1017.upper_bound ask for natural-number lower and upper bounds on f(n, k) for k > n²/4; this asymptotic result over all k does not supply them.
mathematical_sources.title: Formal Conjectures: ErdosProblems/1017.lean

mathematical_sources.identifier: Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969), Academic Press, London (1971), 97–109
mathematical_sources.note: Source of the question, in item 11 on p. 101: whether the Erdős–Goodman–Pósa bound can be sharpened for k > n²/4.
mathematical_sources.title: Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis

mathematical_sources.note: Proves f(n, k) ≤ floor(n²/4), with edges and triangles only; the complete balanced bipartite graph attains it.
mathematical_sources.title: The representation of a graph by set intersections

mathematical_sources.identifier: Combinatorics (Eger, 1987), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 52, North-Holland (1988), 267–276
mathematical_sources.note: Bounds the number of edge-disjoint triangles in graphs with floor(n²/4) + m edges. With the 1991 paper below and the lower-bound graphs of Győri and Keszegh (a triangle-free graph inside one side of the complete balanced bipartite graph), this determines f(n, k) = floor(n²/4) − m for m at most a linear function of n, and gives floor(n²/4) − m + O(m²/n²) for m = o(n²).
mathematical_sources.title: On the number of edge-disjoint triangles in graphs of given size

mathematical_sources.note: Extends the 1988 bounds from triangles to edge-disjoint cliques of every fixed order.
mathematical_sources.title: On the number of edge disjoint cliques in graphs of given size

mathematical_sources.identifier: Sets, Graphs and Numbers (Budapest, 1991), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 60, North-Holland (1992), 357–363
mathematical_sources.title: Edge disjoint cliques in graphs

mathematical_sources.identifier: Theory of Graphs (Proc. Colloq., Tihany, 1966), Academic Press (1968), 231–236
mathematical_sources.note: Treats the covering version, in which the cliques need not be edge-disjoint.
mathematical_sources.title: On covering of graphs

mathematical_sources.note: Every K₄-free graph with floor(n²/4) + m edges has m edge-disjoint triangles. This is sharp for m up to about n²/16: a triangle-free graph with m edges inside one side of the complete balanced bipartite graph attains it, which settles the K₄-free case in that range.
mathematical_sources.title: On the number of edge-disjoint triangles in K₄-free graphs

mathematical_sources.note: Its bound on decompositions into edges and triangles implies f(n, k) ≤ n²/4 − m/3 + o(n²) for k = floor(n²/4) + m.
mathematical_sources.title: Decomposing graphs into edges and triangles

mathematical_sources.note: Sharpens the previous decomposition bound, which gives f(n, k) ≤ (n² − k + 2)/3 for large n. With the theorem, it gives B(d) ≤ (1 − d)/3, and numerical evaluation indicates that the inequality is strict for 1/4 < d ≤ 1/2; neither comparison is checked in Lean.
mathematical_sources.title: Sharp bounds for decomposing graphs into edges and triangles

mathematical_sources.note: Proves Győri's conjecture that, for each fixed r ≥ 3, every n-vertex graph with ℓ edges more than the Turán graph T_{r−1}(n) has (2 − o(1))ℓ/r edge-disjoint r-cliques as n → ∞. The case r = 3 is the Král'–Lidický–Martins–Pehova result, proved again by a different method, so it gives the same bound f(n, k) ≤ n²/4 − m/3 + o(n²).
mathematical_sources.title: Packing edge disjoint cliques in graphs

mathematical_sources.note: Advances in Combinatorics 2026:9. The case of Theorem 1.10 used here, cp(G) ≤ cp*(G) + o(n²) uniformly over graphs on n vertices, is proved in Lean by regularity cleaning, truncation of large cliques, random allocation and a hypergraph nibble; the published theorem is not assumed.
mathematical_sources.title: Clique covers and decompositions of cliques of graphs

mathematical_sources.note: Concurrent work that also uses linear-programming duality for clique decompositions.
mathematical_sources.title: Clique decompositions and covers for large graphs

mathematical_sources.note: An AI-generated working report on Erdős Problem a Day, dated 2026-07-29, not independently verified, that does not solve the problem. It computes f(n, k) exactly for n ≤ 7 by exhaustive search and leaves the behavior at positive excess density open.
mathematical_sources.title: Erdős problem #1017: verified partial results

mathematical_sources.note: The prose account accompanying this repository, in blueprint/; not refereed. It follows the Lean development module by module, proving some steps and cases in full and summarizing the others.
mathematical_sources.title: Uniform asymptotics of clique partition numbers (blueprint)

mathematical_sources.note: The companion paper accompanying this repository, in paper/; not refereed. It proves the shorter parts and one exclusion in full and summarizes the rest, which Lean proves.
mathematical_sources.title: An asymptotic formula for clique partitions above the Turán threshold
